verdicts.strongest_argument: The arithmetic is right — I pulled WPU072106038 from FRED myself and every figure reconciles to the decimal (May/Jun/Jul 2026 = 182.669/184.350/188.565, mean 185.195 vs 186.492 a year earlier = -0.70%; Feb/Mar/Apr 2026 mean 174.951 vs 190.479 = -8.15%; Jul-26 188.565 vs Jul-25 185.009 = +1.92%; +8.24% off the Mar-26 trough of 174.202). The fiscal mapping is also right: CNM FQ1 FY26 = 2 Feb–3 May, FQ2 = 4 May–2 Aug, so Feb/Mar/Apr and May/Jun/Jul are correct. So this is not refutable on the data. It is, however, close to fully anticipated on the transmission, which is the part that matters. Three separate layers of publication: (1) the commodity move itself was mainstream trade press all year — pipe mills took ~10% in late March 2026 (Supply House Times / Plumbing & Mechanical April and July round-ups), US PVC contract prices ran +12–16% in Q2 2026 (ChemAnalyst, openPR tracker), Plastics Technology flagged PVC up in March; (2) the specific July datapoint that carries the +1.9% y/y was published by BLS on 2026-08-13, four weeks before this print; (3) decisively, management narrated exactly this shape on the 10 June Q1 call — Robyn Bradbury said 'we have started to see price increase announcements from our suppliers, but we haven't seen that hit our revenue numbers yet', 'we did do a little buying ahead of price increases on PVC... majority of that would hit in the third quarter', and 'PVC will still be down year-over-year even if we do get some uplift'. That last quote is the hunter's own -0.7% conclusion, pre-stated by the CFO. Gross margin was guided flat at the Q1 exit level of ~27.2% for the balance of the year and FY sales/EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed. What is genuinely NOT drawn out anywhere I can find: the sequential slope is steeper than 'modest' (+3.9% m/m in May alone, +8.2% in four months), and a distributor holding cheap inventory into a fast replacement-cost rise books a holding gain in the quarter the cost rises — that lands in FQ2 gross margin, not FQ3 revenue, and it is the one channel management's 'flat at 27.2%' guide does not obviously capture. Two things cut against sizing it large: PVC pipe is only ~15–20% of CNM revenue, and this PPI is a materially damped proxy for CNM's own realised pricing — CNM told the market in Sept 2025 that municipal PVC pipe was down ~15% y/y at a time WPU072106038 was down ~7.5%, roughly a 2x amplitude gap in the index's disfavour, so the index cannot be used to size the effect cleanly in either direction. I am not scoring this above 80 precisely because the fiscal-quarter re-cut plus the inventory-gain channel is a real residual; I am not scoring it below 60 because the company itself pre-announced the direction, the timing and the caveat.

prior_publication.what_it_says: BLS published the July 2026 PPI (188.565 for plastics sewer/stormdrain/water main pipe) in the 2026-08-13 PPI news release; the whole series is free and continuously public.

CFO Robyn Bradbury: supplier PVC price increase announcements seen, bought ahead of them, 'majority of that would hit in the third quarter', PVC 'will still be down year-over-year even if we do get some uplift', gross margin guided to stay near the 27.2% Q1 exit rate.
Trade press round-up of the ~10% PVC/CPVC pipe mill price increases effective late March 2026, with a further round reported in the July 2026 edition.
US PVC prices jumped 12–16% in Q2 2026, from ~$557/t in Q1 to $624–644/t by June, on supply tightness — the resin move underlying the pipe PPI inflection.
Plastics Technology reported PVC resin prices rising in March 2026, the month of the PPI trough.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Ambiguous, and this is the honest reason I did not go higher. Spot 43.94 sits at a 52-week low (Daily Political flagged a new 52-week low on 2026-09-03), 20-day run-up -5.1%, 25d skew +3.24 vol points with put/call OI 1.11 — the market is paying for downside, not for a pricing-driven margin beat. That positioning says the pricing tailwind is under-weighted relative to the volume worry, which argues for a lower number. But the counter-positioning is about emphasis, not about the fact being unpublished, and 'the market is worried about something else' is not the same as 'nobody has this datapoint'. The 9.22% event implied move is roughly double the 4.48% median realised reaction, i.e. the market is already braced for a large repricing in either direction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that CNM's realised municipal PVC pipe pricing tracked the index's +8.2% sequential rebound rather than the ~2x-damped relationship implied by the Sept-2025 comparison, or a Q1 10-Q inventory disclosure showing a large low-cost pipe position carried into FQ2, would push this toward 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is wire copy. Mueller Water Products released Q3 FY26 on GlobeNewswire on 2026-08-05 and it was covered same-day and next-day by Investing.com (twice, slides and transcript), StockTitan, MarketBeat, Motley Fool, Globe and Mail, Yahoo and AOL. Every number the hunter quotes — $395.9M net sales +4.1%, adjusted EBITDA $107.4M +24.3% with 440bp of margin expansion, adjusted EPS $0.50 +47.1%, FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to $367–372M — is in the press release verbatim, and I verified them against the 8-K exhibit. MWA is CNM's most-covered supplier and closest listed water-infrastructure comp; drawing the read-through is the single most routine thing an analyst covering this space does in the five weeks between the two prints. More importantly, the read-through is not the clean positive it is presented as. MWA's beat came from its own pricing actions plus tariff refunds plus cost management — MWA taking price across most product lines is an increase in CNM's cost of goods, not automatically an increase in CNM's margin, and it only helps CNM if pass-through leads the cost. And MWA reported 'slightly lower volumes', which is a mildly NEGATIVE volume read-through for CNM and sits alongside CNM#2 rather than against it. So the finding is both fully published and directionally contestable in the part that matters for CNM's EPS.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The full MWA Q3 FY26 release with all the figures cited, distributed on the wire.
Same-day coverage headlining record margins and the guidance raise.
Full MWA Q3 call transcript including management's price/cost commentary and the tariff-refund contribution.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: CNM rose 4.05% on 2026-08-03 and 2.33% on 2026-08-07, bracketing the MWA release on 08-05, so if anything the price already took the positive read-through and then gave it all back and more later in August into a 52-week low — the market saw it and decided something else mattered more.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A specific MWA disclosure about distributor destocking or channel inventory at CNM that was not picked up in any of the same-day coverage would move this to 45.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a US Census Bureau macro release. Monthly New Residential Construction for July 2026 came out on 2026-08-18 and was covered by Census itself, HousingWire, TD Economics, Calculated Risk, Trading Economics, Red Book Lumber Data, the Housing Affordability Institute and mortgagenewsdaily — the hunter's own source is a 2026-08-21 recap of a release that was already three days old. I verified the numbers: single-family starts 808k SAAR, -9.9% m/m, total starts 1,239k, -12.4% m/m, permits +5.0%; the figures are right, only the 'lowest since November 2022' tag is not stated in the cited article. Beyond publication, this one is visibly in the price. CNM traded around $47 in early August, fell through the second half of the month, and set a new 52-week low in early September; WallStreetZen cut it to Hold on 2026-08-08 and Northcoast cut it from Buy to Neutral on 2026-08-26, eight days after the housing print. The options agree: 25-delta skew +3.24 vol points with the baseline calling the lean 'downside paid' and put/call open interest at 1.11. A bearish residential finding on a name at a 52-week low with puts bid is agreement with the market, not information. The mechanism also mostly misses the quarter being reported — residential lot development, which is what CNM actually sells into, LEADS starts, so a July starts print reaches this event through the forward guide rather than through the 2 August quarter-end. The only non-obvious sliver is the juxtaposition against management's 10 June 'stable relative to the fourth quarter and in line with our expectations' language, and that juxtaposition is an inference every sell-side preview will have run.

HousingWire covered the July drop in both single-family and multifamily starts on release day.
The hunter's own source, a recap dated three days after the release: 'Single-family starts declined 9.9% to 808k'.
Independent 08-18 dated republication of the same Census release, fixing the actual publication date off the URL path.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Run-up 20d -5.1%, spot 43.94 only 4.44% above the 52-week low and 34% below the 52-week high, a fresh 52-week low on 2026-09-03, two downgrades in August, 25d skew +3.24 vol points and put/call OI 1.11. Every one of those is the market having already absorbed residential deterioration.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If CNM's residential exposure were concentrated in the specific Sun Belt markets driving the July collapse and that geographic split were undisclosed, the guidance risk would be larger than the tape suggests and I would go to 70.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component of this is a separately published document, most of it wire copy, and the composite is a speculation rather than a fact. The notes were priced on 2026-06-25 (8-K pricing press release, plus same-week coverage by Yahoo Finance, Investing.com and TipRanks) and closed 1 July with the closing 8-K filed 2026-07-02, which I fetched and verified — $750M of 6.000% senior notes due 1 July 2034, use of proceeds exactly as quoted. But the same 8-K discloses that this sits alongside a new $800M senior term loan maturing 2033 replacing the 2028 term loan: TipRanks headlined it 'Core & Main refinances debt, extends maturities to 2033', which is the correct characterisation. A refinancing is not incremental M&A/buyback firepower, and the use-of-proceeds language listing 'organic growth, M&A, share repurchases and other initiatives' is boilerplate that appears in essentially every high-yield offering memorandum. The buyback figures ($88M/1.8M shares in Q1, $37M/0.8M in the five weeks to 10 June, $581M remaining on the $1bn authorisation) come from the Q1 10-Q and the 10 June call, public for three months, and the 'notable uptick in the pipeline... to larger opportunities' M&A quote is from that same call. What remains unpublished is only the inference that an unusually large Q2 buyback or a deal will land with tomorrow's print — and that is small even if right: $100M of repurchase against roughly $8.6bn of equity value is about 1% of shares and well under 1% of EPS, and the incremental interest cost of $750M at 6.000% (~$11M/quarter) is roughly a wash against the prepaid floating-rate term loan it replaced.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 8-K press release announcing pricing of the $750M 6.000% senior notes due 2034, with the full use-of-proceeds language including M&A and share repurchases.
Characterises the transaction as a refinancing and maturity extension, not as new firepower.
Closing 8-K confirming issuance on 1 July 2026 and the accompanying new $800M term loan maturing 1 July 2033.
Source of the Q1 buyback figures, the remaining authorisation and the M&A pipeline commentary the finding quotes.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None specific. The notes priced 2026-06-25 and the stock's subsequent path (roughly $47 in early August down to a 52-week low in early September) shows no capital-allocation premium being carried into this print.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: An 8-K or press release confirming a signed acquisition of scale, or a Q2 repurchase materially above the record $88M run-rate, disclosed only with the print, would make this a 30 rather than an 84.

interactions: Three of the four rest partly on the same document, the 10 June 2026 Q1 FY26 earnings call, and it is the document that damages them. CNM#0's entire transmission story was pre-stated there by CFO Robyn Bradbury — supplier increases seen, bought ahead, 'majority of that would hit in the third quarter', 'PVC will still be down year-over-year even if we do get some uplift', gross margin guided flat at ~27.2% — which means the hunter's computed -0.7% FQ2 y/y is a confirmation of guidance rather than a departure from it, and pushes most of the benefit into FQ3 (Aug–Oct), outside the quarter being reported. CNM#2's counterpoint quote and CNM#3's buyback and M&A-pipeline figures come from that same call and 10-Q. Second, CNM#0 and CNM#1 are not independent: they are the same 'waterworks pricing is inflecting up' thesis read off two instruments, and they partly cancel — Mueller raising price across most product lines is CNM's cost of goods rising, so MWA's margin expansion is only a CNM positive to the extent CNM out-passes it, and MWA's 'slightly lower volumes' is a mild negative that sits with CNM#2, not against it. Third, CNM#0 and CNM#2 are direct mirrors: price up, volume down, both landing on the same FY guidance decision tomorrow, and management's 10 June cadence guide ('slight growth in the second quarter, low to mid-single-digit in the third and fourth') is the single number both must be measured against. Ranking this name on CNM#0 alone without netting CNM#2 would double-count one side of one question.
